amorem 1.3.0 — pre-release audit (2026-11-19)

Source: AUDIT.md

State reviewed: main at 4bfc31a. R CMD check --as-cran (R 4.4.0, macOS): 0 errors, 0 warnings, 2 NOTEs (installed size 5.4 MB; time server unreachable). Reverse dependencies on CRAN: none.

Every finding below was reproduced by running the code shown. Items marked ✔ were re-run a second time independently.

Verified correct: rem(method = "clogit") equals survival::clogit (coefficients and logLik); gam with one control equals clogit; compare_models() equals clogit; martingale residuals equal survival’s to 2e-9; gof_rem() has size 0.03–0.07 under the null and power 1.0 against nonlinear and time-varying effects; the Gillespie and tau-leap simulators recover count, binary, transitivity and outdegree effects within Monte Carlo error; the 64 C++ statistics match the R implementation on logs without tied times; no sampler draws a loop, an excluded pair or the event dyad itself; seeds restore the caller’s RNG state.

A. Wrong results with no error (fix before release)

  1. ✔ Pure-R feature path: a control sees its own event. R/preprocess.R:872–1003. Requesting any R-only statistic (reciprocity_exp_decay, reciprocity_time_recent, reciprocity_time_first, reciprocity_*_interrupted) sends all requested statistics through a row-by-row loop that adds each event to the history before its same-time controls are computed. The C++ path reads a whole timestamp before writing.

    cc <- data.frame(stratum=c(1,1,2,2,3,3), event=c(1,0,1,0,1,0),
  sender=c("A","B","C","B","B","A"), receiver=c("B","A","D","A","A","C"), time=c(1,1,2,2,3,3))
endogenous_features(cc, "reciprocity")$reciprocity                               # 0 0 0 1 1 0
endogenous_features(cc, c("reciprocity","reciprocity_time_recent"))$reciprocity  # 0 1 0 1 1 0

    With tied times and a history mask the two engines also differ on outdegree, reciprocity_count and the triadic statistics (63 of 300 rows for sender_outdegree).

  2. ✔ history_log / prior_log count same-time controls as events. R/preprocess.R:407–409, 534–541. Events are identified by matching (sender, receiver, time); under the default risk = "standard" a control may equal another stratum’s event at the same time.

    E <- data.frame(sender=c("A","C","A"), receiver=c("B","D","E"), time=c(1,1,2))
cc <- sample_non_events(E, 3, seed = 17)        # stratum 2 draws control A->B at t = 1
endogenous_features(cc, "sender_outdegree", history_log = E)  # row 9 (A->E, t=2): 2; true 1

  3. ✔ scope = "appearance" admits actors first seen at the same time. R/preprocess.R:1497–1499 updates the pool per row, not per timestamp.

    toy <- data.frame(sender=c("A","C","E"), receiver=c("B","D","F"), time=c(1,1,2))
sample_non_events(toy, 3, scope = "appearance", seed = 1)   # stratum 2 (t=1) gets A->B, B->A

    67 such controls in classroom_events with 5 controls per event.

  4. sample_non_events() assumes a time-sorted log. R/preprocess.R:1460–1504. Appearance and risk = "remove" follow row order.

    toy2 <- data.frame(sender=c("C","A","B"), receiver=c("D","B","A"), time=c(3,1,2))
sample_non_events(toy2, 2, scope="appearance", risk="remove", seed=1)  # t=1 gets D->C

  5. ✔ A factor event column inverts cases and controls. R/rem.R:174, 218, 489, R/widen_case_control.R:69, R/rem_nn_uncertainty.R:49: as.integer(factor(c("0","1"))) is 1 2. method = "nn" trains on reversed labels; clogit without a stratum column gets wrong strata; widen_case_control() errors.

  6. ✔ nn_uncertainty() rebuilds case from the formula. R/rem_nn_uncertainty.R:44, 47; rem() does not store case / stratum. With rem(~ x + y, case = "event") the bootstrap uses x as the event indicator (concordance 0.18 against the fit’s 0.86).

  7. ✔ compare_models_global() never uses the last grid value. R/compare_models_global.R:214: findInterval(..., all.inside = TRUE) maps t ≥ last grid time to the second-to-last value. The package example’s grid ends at max(time). Fix: pmax(findInterval(t, g$time[ord]), 1L).

  8. rem() drops offset() terms silently (gam and clogit). R/rem.R:142 reads only term.labels. Support them or stop when attr(terms(f), "offset") is set.

  9. ✔ Simulator: length-1 sample() gives invalid controls. R/simulate_events.R:1593 (Gillespie), :1368 (tau-leap), R/simulate_directed_hyperevents_tvnl.R:166. With one candidate left, sample(k, 1) draws from 1:k. Two actors, n_controls = 1: 85 of 200 controls are loops, 37 equal their case. Use x[sample.int(length(x), n)].

  10. ✔ Simulator: overflowing intensity drops the dyad. R/simulate_events.R:688, 1223, 1497 set non-finite weights to 0, so exp(710) becomes rate 0 (A->B fires 0 of 20 times; with 700, 20 of 20). Underflow shrinks the control pool and raises “n_controls >= admissible dyads”. Compute weights as exp(log_w - max(log_w)).

  11. ✔ Simulator: exp-decay statistics are chosen from undecayed state. R/simulate_events.R:1491–1512 against :1565–1569: rates come from the state at the previous event and decay is applied after the new time is drawn. reciprocity_exp_decay with effect 1.5, half-life 0.5 is recovered as 2.22–2.69 (SE ≈ 0.11) over 5 replicates. Recency and *_time_* statistics carry the same mismatch with negligible bias (0.201–0.203 for 0.2).

  12. simulate_directed_hyperevents_tvnl() can pass horizon (:146–153, last step not capped; max time 1.0048 with horizon = 1). Its docs call the scheme “thinning”; it is a piecewise-constant midpoint rate.

  13. standardize_event_log() with factor or text times. R/preprocess.R:73–81: a factor time becomes level codes ("10" sorts before "2"); text dates become NA and drop_nas = TRUE returns 0 rows with only a coercion warning.

B. Hangs, errors and reproducibility

  1. ✔ NA time hangs R (also a CRAN risk). src/compute_features_cpp.cpp:987–989: times[g_end] == times[g] is never true for NaN. Reached whenever the history mask is on (controls present, history_log or prior_log).

    ev <- data.frame(sender=c("A","B","C"), receiver=c("B","A","A"), time=c(1,2,NA))
endogenous_features(ev, "reciprocity", history_log = ev)   # never returns

    sample_non_events() keeps NA-time rows, so it can produce such data.

  2. max_attempts aborts valid runs under risk = "remove" (R/preprocess.R:1473–1486); the ordinary branch lacks the full-enumeration fallback the shift branch has. One species, 3000 regions, mode = "two": “Unable to sample a valid non-event after 1000 attempts”.

  3. torch with batch_strata is not reproducible on the first fit of a session (R/rem_nn.R:331): loading torch consumes RNG draws after set.seed(). Call requireNamespace("torch") before seeding.

  4. shift = "exponential": fails on Date/POSIXct times (R/preprocess.R:1416) and on a log with a single timestamp (default window has start = end); returns before the documented no_control warning.

  5. re(x) with a single column (documented fallback) crashes inside mgcv (chol.default ... 'a' must have dims > 0); the term is identically zero.

  6. tau-leap records the cyclic, sending- and receiving-balance *_time_*_ordered statistics at step start (R/simulate_events.R:1281–1301); transitivity’s is recorded at event time.

C. Documentation, data and CRAN polish

  1. ✔ alien_invasions docs say 272 regions; the data has 259 (R/data.R:339). Same block: 407 rows have start == stop with stop != 1880, against the stated rule.
  2. classroom_events$weight documented as integer (values 0.2, 1); social_evolution_actors$gradeType levels are “1”–“5”, not names; social_evolution_calls spans 2008-09-06 to 2008-10-18, not the 2008–09 year.
  3. No licence stated for classroom_* (networkDynamic, GPL), social_evolution_* (goldfish), college_msg, email_eu_core (SNAP), in an MIT package whose cran-comments says every dataset’s licence allows redistribution.
  4. gof_multivariate, gof_global, gof_auxiliary, nn_control, nn_uncertainty have no examples; the rem and gof_rem examples use mgcv without a guard.
  5. gam on long data with several controls keeps only the first control, and says only that it widens (R/rem.R:245).
  6. predict() on gam fits needs internal column names in newdata; not listed under @return.
  7. transform_recency(half_life = T) uses T as the e-folding scale (weight 0.368 at T, not 0.5).
  8. Controls are drawn with replacement (duplicates in small risk sets), undocumented; n_controls = 1.5 and n_events = 2.7 are truncated silently; clogit fits report n = nrow(data) including NA rows and have no $rows.

D. Questions on intended behaviour

  • scope = "citation" draws control receivers only from papers that have already cited something, so papers that are only ever cited are never controls, and every event at the first timestamp gets no control (R/preprocess.R:1279–1284). Intended?
  • Tied times without a mask: events at one timestamp see each other in row order (A->B and B->A at t = 1 give reciprocity 0 1); with a mask they give 0 0. Which is the definition?
  • Under risk = "remove" the new no-control warning fires on ordinary data (events 2–3 of classroom_events, whose pool is still tiny). Keep it, or exempt the first timestamps?
